use: The district map: hangs in the frame on the wall, and is the ground of the road screen
subject: A Survey of India district sheet of the 1920s, printed from an engraved plate — a single district about forty miles across, filling the sheet. Dense with survey detail: tehsil boundaries drawn as fine dot-and-dash lines dividing the district into six parts; a broad meandering river with sandbanks and a ferry, crossed by a girder bridge; two irrigation canals with their distributaries branching off in fine lines; a metalled road drawn as a firm double line and a web of unmetalled cart tracks in single lines; a single-track railway drawn as a line with cross-ties, with three small station symbols along it; a range of hills across one corner rendered in fine hachures, the strokes running down the slope and heavier where it is steep; scattered village symbols as small open circles with a stipple of huts; mango groves as little tufted symbols; tanks and jheels as closed shapes with ruled water lines inside them; a forest reserve marked by even stipple; marsh symbols along one bank. A ruled border with fine graduation ticks all round, an ornamental north point, and a blank scale bar. Everything in one warm black ink on buff paper.
